instruction: Change the video aspect ratio in VLC to 16:9 format.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing VLC aspect ratio to 16:9. Agent can use Video > Aspect Ratio menu. Custom getter reads aspect ratio information from VLC HTTP status.xml, metric performs string comparison.
metadata.verification: VLC aspect ratio options include default, 16:9, 4:3, 16:10, etc. Getter extracts aspect ratio from status.xml video metadata.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Getter reads video file metadata, not VLC UI setting - The getter queries 'Display aspect ratio' from status.xml video metadata (vlc.py:31-35), which extracts the video file's inherent aspect ratio, NOT the VLC UI aspect ratio setting that users change via Video > Aspect Ratio menu

Semantic mismatch: Instruction requires verifying UI setting change, but getter reads video stream properties - When users change aspect ratio via VLC menu, they apply a display override that doesn't modify the video file's metadata. The getter will likely always return the video's original aspect ratio regardless of UI settings

State accessibility issue: VLC's HTTP status.xml may not expose user-selected aspect ratio override settings - The status.xml typically contains video stream metadata and playback state, but not UI override settings like forced aspect ratio

Incomplete verification: Evaluator cannot detect whether the instruction was completed - Even if the user successfully changes VLC's aspect ratio setting to 16:9, the getter will continue reading the video file's inherent aspect ratio, making verification impossible
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Alternative approach 1: Use VLC command-line query or dbus interface to read the actual aspect ratio setting (not video metadata)
Alternative approach 2: Use accessibility tree or UI inspection to verify the aspect ratio menu selection state
Alternative approach 3: Parse VLC's config file or preferences where aspect ratio overrides might be stored

Verify that the chosen approach reads the UI setting, not the video file's inherent properties - test with a video that has a different native aspect ratio than 16:9 to ensure the getter detects the UI setting change
